benchmark_metadata.title: System-Level Supreme Court Jurisprudence Benchmark Evaluation (Tier 3)

case_level_results.case_name: Mosqueda v. Pilipino Banana Growers & Exporters Association, Inc.
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Under the Magtajas doctrine, an ordinance cannot prohibit an activity expressly permitted or regulated by national law. PD 1144 vests exclusive jurisdiction in the Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority to regulate agricultural chemical application methods.

case_level_results.case_name: Hon. Leoncio Evasco, Jr. v. Alex P. Montañez
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(4)(iv); Presidential Decree No. 1096 §301
case_level_results.judicial_ruling: Constitutional and Valid Exercise of Police Power (Upheld)
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Under RA 7160 §458(a)(4)(iv), city councils possess explicit statutory police power to regulate advertising displays and signboards, harmoniously complementing the National Building Code.

case_level_results.case_name: City of Davao and Tanjili v. ARC Investors, Inc.
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §143(f); Republic Act No. 8791 §3
case_level_results.legal_rationale: A holding company passively earning dividend income is not a non-bank financial intermediary without express Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas licensing. LGUs cannot redefine statutory banking categories.

case_level_results.case_name: City of Davao and Dureza v. First Meridian Development, Inc.
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Section 195 of the Local Government Code governing business taxes deliberately does not require payment under protest. Local councils cannot impose restrictive procedural preconditions not authorized by statute.

case_level_results.case_name: City of Davao v. Court of Appeals and GSIS
case_level_results.ordinance_no: Davao City Real Property Tax Assessment on GSIS
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Sections 193 and 234 of RA 7160 expressly withdrew prior real property tax exemptions of government-owned or controlled corporations, making Davao City's municipal tax assessment a lawful exercise of delegated authority.

case_level_results.case_name: Davao City Mining Ban and Panigan-Tamugan Watershed Dispute
case_level_results.judicial_ruling: Active Vertical Preemption / Ultra Vires under Magtajas
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Under the Magtajas doctrine, an ordinance cannot forbid what national law permits. Blanket territorial bans on mining collide directly with national statutory concessions under RA 7942.

case_level_results.case_name: Davao City Comprehensive Anti-Smoking Ordinance vs. National Standards
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Republic Act No. 9211 §5
case_level_results.legal_rationale: National health statutes establish minimum baseline standards, not maximum ceilings. Stricter local health measures under police power are valid provided they do not legalize what national law prohibits.

case_level_results.case_name: Davao City Comprehensive Speed Limit Ordinance under Joint JAO 2018-01
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Republic Act No. 4136 §35, §38; Joint DILG-DOTr-DPWH JAO 2018-01
case_level_results.legal_rationale: National traffic statutes and Joint JAO 2018-01 expressly delegate speed classification and local road rate-setting powers to local government units.

case_level_results.case_name: Magtajas v. Pryce Properties Corp. and PAGCOR
case_level_results.ordinance_no: Cagayan de Oro Ord. No. 3353 & Ord. No. 3375-93
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1869 §1; Republic Act No. 7160 §5(a)
case_level_results.judicial_ruling: Ordinances Null and Void / Foundational Preemption Ruling (Overturned)
case_level_results.legal_rationale: An ordinance cannot permit what a statute forbids, nor forbid what a statute permits. Local councils are merely delegated agents of the national legislature.

case_level_results.case_name: City of Manila v. Laguio, Jr.
case_level_results.controlling_statute: 1987 Constitution, Article III, Section 1; Republic Act No. 7160 §458
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Prohibiting lawful commercial businesses instead of regulating them violates substantive due process. Local police power cannot arbitrarily destroy legitimate enterprises.

case_level_results.case_name: Batangas CATV, Inc. v. Court of Appeals
case_level_results.ordinance_no: Batangas SP Resolution No. 210, Series of 1993
case_level_results.controlling_statute: Executive Order No. 205 §2; Executive Order No. 546 §15
case_level_results.judicial_ruling: Resolution and Rate-Fixing Powers Struck Down (Overturned)
case_level_results.legal_rationale: Executive orders vest exclusive regulatory and rate-fixing authority over cable television in the National Telecommunications Commission. Where national law occupies the regulatory field, municipal ordinances are preempted.
